Passes #32, #37 and #42 held rung 4 for one reason — the town had no night — and that climb is now landed: windows keep hours (#39), the door has callers (#47), the river has lamps and a night stander (#46), and snow (#45) gave winter a wide-shot tell. Every brief here wires two things that already exist and ignore each other. b45 goes first because it is a defect a thirty-second viewer sees: the whole picture relights in one frame at winter dusk (5–9 whole-frame Δ on HEAD, twice what any feature produces) because the cached ground repaints on a quarter-hour bucket that is coarse exactly where the light moves fastest. b46 is snow × the one system the courtyard is famous for (desire paths) plus the sweeper who already exists — the cheapest legible winter connection, in the most starved domain. b47 gives the plaza the wind, the one scalar nothing east of the bridge reads (WATCH). b48 is the bet: the town's people leave the frame at dusk and nobody goes HOME — a walker who turns in at a door and lights the window they went to is the single thing that would make the night read as inhabited rather than decorated; it touches the cached facade layer, WINDOWS[] and routeToExit, and it can fail. b49 gives the allotments a winter (the block is empty for a quarter of the year: allotRate floors at 0.01 with ripePlots 0). queue.brief: Snow (#45, `snowCover`, `snowAt(x,y,t)` at ~1011) and foot wear (`wear[]`, written at ~1822 by every walker step, read by `drawGround` at ~3388 for desire paths) do not know each other: a lying cover whitens the lawn evenly and the town's most-loved emergent feature — the paths people wear — vanishes for a quarter of the year. `snowAt` already takes less on trodden KINDS; extend that to the wear VALUE so a worn line through the lawn stays dark through the snow and a fresh cover is re-trodden from the arches inward over a morning. Then give the pre-dawn sweeper (~2320, `sweeper`) a winter job: the strip they sweep (their actual route) is cleared, so at dawn on a snowy day there is one swept path and the rest is white until feet cut the desire paths again.
queue.successLooksLike: A winter-morning shot (seed 7, snowCover > 0.4) shows dark desire paths through a white lawn and one swept strip; the same instant on HEAD is an even white. Summer frames byte-identical to HEAD. A probe over five seed-winters: mean snow on cells with wear > 0.45 is under half the mean on cells with wear < 0.1. snow-year.mjs's cover means move less than 5%.
queue.avoid: Do not add a new ground kind or a new R() draw. Wear is per courtyard cell only — do not invent wear for the paved east. Keep the repaint on SNOW_REPAINT steps; a per-frame ground redraw is the one thing that would fail perf.

queue.brief: `isWindy()` (~842) moves washing, smoke, leaves, tree sway and the morning ticker line — all west of the bridge. The fountain (`drawFountain` ~4404) sprays five symmetric jets in a gale. Make the plaza read a windy day: the jets lean and their droplets carry downwind (there is a `windT`/`sway` already at ~3815 to phase off), the lee side of the basin gets a visible drift of spray, and `fountainStand()` (the share willing to stand at it, read by both spawners) drops on windy days so people take the benches instead of the wet side. If budget allows, the bandstand bunting (`bandF`) flutters on the same days.
queue.successLooksLike: Two shots at the same pinned instant, one windy day and one calm (pick days by hash(day,99)): the windy plume visibly leans one way and the calm one is symmetric. fountain-year.mjs still passes at the anchor. Over ten windy days, standers at the fountain are measurably fewer than on ten calm days, with the bench share up by the same amount (the east's arrivals are unchanged).
queue.avoid: No new R() draws in the renderer — lean and drift are hash()+clock. Do not change eastCap/eastRate; move the SPLIT, not the arrivals. Do not touch the river streaks (they drift on riverRun and that is the river's job).

queue.brief: Nobody in this town goes home. `routeToExit()` (~1677) walks every leaver off the frame, and the windows (`windowLit` ~2942, hash-only, per night) light on their own with no one behind them. Connect them: a share of the walkers who leave after dusk (nightF > 0.3) instead walk to a DOOR on a cached facade that has a window above it, vanish into it, and THAT window's pane lights at that moment (a small live register keyed by (sa,sb), read by windowLit alongside its hash, repainted by drawLitPanes which already runs per frame) and keeps that window's normal bedtime. The evening door (`TAP_DOOR`, `drawTapDoor`) is the pattern for a door on `drawFaceRow`; pick 4–8 doors along the lane and the courtyard's own facades, each with a window over it. Price the walk with pathHours() first — a walker who cannot reach the door before their window's own `on` hour goes off-frame as now.
queue.successLooksLike: On a night filmstrip a figure walks to a door, disappears, and a window above it lights in the same second — visible at 1x. Over ten seed-nights at least a third of dusk leavers go to a door, and every window lit by an arrival is one windowLit would have allowed that night (no window lit that is 'nobody home'). windows-night.mjs's lit fractions move under 10%. personName says 'heading home'. The swans, while there: rest on the bank at nightF > 0.6 (cue c75) — one line in updateSwans, not a system.
queue.avoid: Do not make windows an agent system. One register, one predicate: windowLit stays the ONE truth and reads the register. No R() in the renderer. Do not send the east's leavers (eastOpenFor) — their walk is priced out; lane and courtyard leavers only.

queue.brief: The allotment block is empty for a quarter of the year: `allotRate = (0.01 + 0.16*ripePlots()/17) * (raining ? 0.2 : 1)` (~5630) and ripePlots() is 0 all winter, so the 0.01 floor sends nobody for ~six sim days and the plots sit under snow with nothing happening in them. Give the block a winter: on mild, dry, daylit winter days (warmth low, !raining, snowCover < 0.3) a gardener comes to a FALLOW plot (bAge as the fallow clock, `harvestPlot`, `plotCrop`) and turns it — an `act:'dig'` stop of a few seconds — and the plot reads as freshly turned earth (a darker, rowless state through `groundCol`/the plot draw) until the spring sowing. Hardy cabbages (`plotStands`) stand through it as they do now.
queue.successLooksLike: allot-year.mjs folded over two years: gardener visits in winter weeks go from ~0 to a small steady rate (1–3 per sim day on dry mild days, 0 in snow or rain), with the summer rate unchanged. A late-winter shot shows two or three dark turned plots among the white/fallow ones; the same instant on HEAD is uniform. Census planting.harvested unchanged.
queue.avoid: Do not change ripePlots() or the harvest cycle. Keep the winter gardener on spawnAllotAgent's own source (it exists so the block does not compete for laneCap). One new per-plot state at most.
